title: Orbit product contract v1
description: A product contract: capabilities and systems (entities) with behaviors, typed relationships and automated tests. Arrays are unordered; items are identified by stable ids.

entities.description: Capabilities and systems, stored flat; hierarchy is expressed with parentId.

relationships.description: Directed typed edges between entities (source -> target).

tests.description: Automated test definitions that behaviors reference.

flows.description: Optional named walkthroughs of how a capability works: an ordered walk along existing relationships. Unlike other arrays, the order of steps within a flow is meaningful.

product.description: The product described by this contract.

entity.description: A node in the unified model: a user-facing capability or an internal system.

id.description: Stable opaque entity id, unique among entities. Never changes on rename or reorder.

kind.description: capability = user-facing product ability; system = internal supporting component.

parentId.description: Id of the parent entity (must exist and have the same kind), or null for a root.

behavior.description: A first-class guarantee: a statement of expected outcome owned by exactly one entity.

id.description: Behavior id, unique across all behaviors in the contract.

expected.description: The expected outcome, as a plain statement.

testIds.description: Ids of tests that verify this behavior (order is not significant). May be empty.

items.description: A test id from the top-level tests array.

relationship.description: A directed typed edge from source to target.

id.description: Stable relationship id, unique among relationships.

type.description: dependsOn: source relies on target functionality; uses: source uses target as support; implementedBy: source capability is supported by target system.

sourceId.description: Id of the source entity (the consumer).

targetId.description: Id of the target entity (the provider). Must differ from sourceId.

id.description: Stable test id, unique among tests.

location.description: Source path, test identifier or URL; not required to exist locally. For a placeholder, where the test is intended to live.

placeholder.description: Present (true) when the test is planned but not implemented yet, e.g. proposed alongside a behavior. Omit once the test exists. A placeholder never counts as test coverage.

flow.description: A named, ordered walk along existing relationships that explains how a capability works, drawn as a sequence diagram.

id.description: Stable flow id, unique among flows. Prefix 'flow.'.

capabilityId.description: Id of the capability this flow explains (must be a capability).

trigger.description: What the user does to start the flow; drawn as User -> capability.

flowStep.description: One step of a flow: travels along an existing relationship.

id.description: Step id, unique within its flow.

relationshipId.description: Id of an existing relationship. A forward step runs source -> target.

reply.description: Present (true) when the step is a reply travelling target -> source along the same relationship. Omit otherwise.

label.description: Optional short text drawn on the arrow, e.g. 'Save task'. Defaults to the relationship's verb ('uses', 'is implemented by', ...) or 'replies'.

description.description: What happens in this step, in plain language.

validation.description: How to validate the product: the command that runs the whole test suite, and where it writes its results. Orbit runs the command only when a person asks it to, and reads test outcomes from the results file.

command.description: Shell command that runs the entire test suite, run from the repository root (or the contract's folder outside Git), e.g. 'npm test'.

results.description: Path of the JUnit XML results file the command writes, relative to the same folder, e.g. 'test-results/junit.xml'.
